entities.summary:
Aminah bint Wahb ibn Abd Manaf al-Zuhriyya, a woman of the Banu Zuhra clan within the powerful Quraish tribe of Mecca, holds a pivotal yet tragically brief role in world history as the mother of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. Born in Mecca around the mid-6th century CE, her significance is entirely derived from her biological connection to the founder of Islam, a religion that would transform the Near East and ripple across continents, shaping civilizations for over 1,400 years. Her lineage connected her to a respected branch of the Quraish, a tribe that dominated the religious and economic life of pre-Islamic Mecca, positioning her within the elite social fabric of the nascent Islamic world.

Aminah's life, largely unrecorded outside of Islamic tradition, is primarily known through accounts detailing her marriage to Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the chosen son of the influential Quraish chieftain Abd al-Muttalib. This union, arranged according to tribal customs, was intended to strengthen alliances and produce heirs. Tragically, Abdullah died just months after their marriage, either before or shortly after Muhammad’s conception, during a trade journey to Yathrib (later Medina). Aminah subsequently gave birth to Muhammad in Mecca around 570 CE. Her widowhood and the subsequent orphanhood of her son, compounded by the custom of sending infants to be nursed in the desert, marked the early, formative years of the future prophet.
